question: What should I do after a relapse in recovery?
intent: Find next steps after returning to substance use
why_this_adds_coverage: Relapse questions are common but require non-shaming, practical guidance. This adds recovery-stage coverage beyond first-time help seeking.

source_refs.title: Treatment and Recovery
source_refs.note: Would support relapse-aware recovery framing and evidence-based treatment options.

notes: Include urgent care guidance if overdose risk, withdrawal danger, or self-harm thoughts are present.

question: How can I support someone who is struggling with addiction without enabling them?
intent: Help a loved one while maintaining boundaries
why_this_adds_coverage: Adds family-and-supporter content for addiction, not just person-centered recovery content. It can distinguish support, boundaries, and crisis escalation.

source_refs.title: National Helpline
source_refs.note: Would support referral pathways for substance use support and treatment navigation.

notes: Avoid simplistic enablement language that blames families.

question: Is it normal to feel bored or empty after getting sober?
intent: Understand emotional adjustment in early recovery
why_this_adds_coverage: Addresses a nuanced recovery experience that may otherwise be missed by treatment-entry content. It can connect emotional flatness with support, routines, and care.

source_refs.title: Treatment and Recovery
source_refs.note: Would support recovery as an ongoing process involving behavioral and social supports.

notes: Flag crisis language if emptiness includes suicidal thoughts.

question: When should someone seek professional help for substance use?
intent: Identify thresholds for getting addiction-related care
why_this_adds_coverage: Provides a broad doorway into treatment navigation for users unsure whether their use qualifies as serious. Useful for early intervention coverage.

source_refs.title: Substance Use
source_refs.note: Would support general substance use information and help-seeking pathways.

notes: Mention emergency help for overdose, severe withdrawal, or immediate danger.

question: How can I tell the difference between stress and anxiety?
why_this_adds_coverage: A high-volume comparison question that can clarify everyday stress versus persistent anxiety. Helps users decide whether support may be needed.

source_refs.title: Anxiety Disorders
source_refs.note: Would support anxiety symptom and impairment descriptions.

question: What can I do when I feel anxious for no clear reason?
intent: Find grounding and next steps for unexplained anxiety
why_this_adds_coverage: Serves users who experience anxiety without an obvious trigger. Adds practical, non-diagnostic anxiety coverage.

source_refs.title: I'm So Stressed Out!
source_refs.note: Would support stress response education and when to seek help.

notes: Include medical caveat for sudden severe physical symptoms.

question: Why do I overthink every conversation after it happens?
why_this_adds_coverage: Adds social-rumination coverage distinct from generalized worry. It can bridge anxiety and communication content without creating a new category.

source_refs.title: Anxiety Disorders
source_refs.note: Would support anxiety symptoms and social anxiety context.

notes: Avoid labeling the user as having social anxiety unless framed as a possibility to discuss with a clinician.

question: Can chronic stress affect my mental health?
why_this_adds_coverage: Adds foundational stress education with broad internal linking potential. Supports prevention-oriented mental health content.

source_refs.title: Stress
source_refs.note: Would support general stress effects and coping guidance.

notes: Keep distinct from workplace burnout pages by focusing on stress broadly.

question: How do I bring up a hard topic without starting a fight?
intent: Start a difficult conversation more constructively
why_this_adds_coverage: Covers proactive conflict prevention rather than repair after conflict. Useful across romantic, family, and workplace contexts.

source_refs.title: Conflict Resolution
source_refs.note: Would support constructive conflict and communication principles.

notes: Avoid implying users can control another person's reaction.

question: What should I do when someone shuts down during conflict?
intent: Respond to withdrawal or silence during disagreement
why_this_adds_coverage: Adds coverage for conflict withdrawal, a common dynamic not captured by anger-focused questions. Helps users distinguish pause, avoidance, and emotional flooding.

source_refs.title: Conflict Resolution
source_refs.note: Would support communication strategies during disagreement.

notes: Use neutral language; do not pathologize shutdown.
